title: Law of total probability over the fibers of a random variable
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite measurable space equipped with a finite measure $\mu$, let $\alpha$ be a finite set, let $Z : \Omega \to \alpha$ be a measurable ($\alpha$-valued) map, and let $S \subseteq \Omega$. Writing $\mu^{\bbr}$ for the real-valued measure and $\mu[\,\cdot \mid A\,]$ for the measure conditioned on an event $A$, we have
\[
  \mu^{\bbr}(S)
  \;=\; \sum_{z \in \alpha} \mu^{\bbr}\bigl(Z^{-1}(\{z\})\bigr)\,
        \cdot\, \mu\bigl[\,\cdot \mid Z^{-1}(\{z\})\,\bigr]^{\bbr}(S),
\]
so the total mass of $S$ is recovered by summing, over the values $z$ of $Z$, the mass of the fiber $Z^{-1}(\{z\})$ times the conditional mass of $S$ given that fiber.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite (and discrete) measurable space
α is a finite type with the discrete σ-algebra
μ is a finite measure on Ω
Z is an α-valued map on Ω
S is a subset of Ω
replaced:
Let $Z : \Omega \to \alpha$ be a finite-valued random variable on a finite measurable
space with finite measure $\mu$, and let $S \subseteq \Omega$.  Then
\[
  \mu^{\mathbb{R}}(S)
  \;=\; \sum_{z \in \alpha} \mu^{\mathbb{R}}(Z^{-1}\{z\})
        \cdot \mu\bigl[\,\cdot \mid Z^{-1}\{z\}\bigr]^{\mathbb{R}}(S).
\]
This is the law of total probability expressed in real-valued measure notation.
